entries.note: The revenue explanation is explicitly conjectural: “I imagine.” His earlier prediction and subsequent promotion of loops are separately checkable.
The explanation rests on executives having no other ideas or abilities. Spending totals alone cannot settle that claimed private motivation.
It explains the investments through their effects and an explicitly imagined belief. Customer rankings and revenue streams are separately checkable.

entries.test: Public accounts of companies building internal replacements for SAP, Salesforce or Office 365, together with contemporaneous market reporting and stock reactions to that narrative, would test the claim.
entries.note: The categorical denial of internal replacements is falsifiable despite the surrounding invective.

entries.test: Public infrastructure contracts, financial disclosures and spending breakdowns would show whether the funding flows through the named hyperscalers into NVIDIA GPU purchases as claimed.
entries.note: The proposition asserts a funding mechanism, not merely infrastructure ownership.

entries.test: Public transaction reporting, model benchmarks, chatbot reception data and Microsoft financial disclosures would test the acquisition cost and claimed results.
entries.note: “Little to show” and “universally-loathed” are evaluative embellishments around concrete claims.

entries.test: Representative public awareness surveys, company product announcements and reporting on OpenAI's founder hire would test the claimed obscurity and corporate adoption pattern.
entries.note: “Which is why” adds a causal explanation. The numerical awareness claim and named corporate actions remain testable.
“Everybody vaguely came to the consensus” that “something would change” supplies no shared standard for testing this explanation.

entries.test: Public procurement timelines and documented corporate decision accounts would test whether Microsoft's GPU purchases drove Amazon, Google and Meta to make theirs.
entries.note: This has a plain reading as a claim about competitive responses in purchasing.

entries.test: Public funding, acquisition and infrastructure agreements, alongside competitors' training and inference capacity, would test the claimed resources and exclusive operating scale.
entries.note: The hyperscaler comparison is grounded in concrete claims about financing and capacity.

entries.test: Public financial statements and funding disclosures would show whether OpenAI and Anthropic can sustain operations from customer revenue without continuing external financing.
entries.note: “Infinite resources” is hyperbole with a plain financial reading: dependence on continuing outside funding.
This is a counterfactual about all AI startups abruptly disappearing, rather than a prediction that this event will occur.
The loss comparison is checkable, but the combined proposition also asserts an unrestricted judgment of superior usefulness. “May have lost money” functions as a concession here.
It attributes private assumptions and motives to every AI lab and startup. Their initial subscription pricing is separately checkable.

entries.test: The cited scaling paper, public training-investment accounts and the documented development chronology of Claude Code and Codex would test the asserted technical rationale and copying.
entries.note: “As much money as they could” adds a claim of spending to their maximum capacity that the source does not state.
The central explanation assigns a private promotional purpose to the giveaways. Product similarities and free-access offers are separately observable.
“Perhaps” presents this as one possible explanation among several. The normalized proposition preserves that hedge.
The exclusive purpose and deliberate concealment are claims about intention. The annualization method and inclusion of non-recurring spending are separately checkable.

entries.test: Publicly released accounting records, audited expense breakdowns or documented reclassifications would show whether OpenAI placed inference costs in sales and marketing and altered its presentation of costs.
entries.note: “I believe” introduces an asserted accounting allegation, rather than an explicit chance or possibility. Records could settle the accounting treatment even if they are not public yet.
